title: 2. The Misleading Shadow
description: Chapter 2 of 3 of “The Case of the Missing Star”. Read in order.

cover.alt: The Case of the Missing Star

illustration.alt: The shadow changes; they knock, and Pico opens with a lantern near a coat stand.

lines: Luna and Nico are still outside the workshop window.
A shadow can look enormous even when the object making it is much smaller than they imagine.
blocks.title: At the workshop door

lines: The light inside shifts, and the silhouette changes at the same moment.
Luna notices the connection: perhaps they should investigate the light as well as the shape.
blocks.title: The shadow shifts

lines: Nico knocks while Luna waits beside him.
They want to find out what is inside rather than turn an unsettling first impression into a certain conclusion.
blocks.title: Knocking

lines: Pico opens the door carrying a lantern.
Behind him stands a coat rack with a purple coat, whose hooks and sleeves make the strange shape on the window.
blocks.title: Pico opens up

variants.retryFeedback: Notice what Pico is carrying and what stands behind him.

variants.prompt: Which question helps them check their first impression?

options.text: What object and light make the shadow
How to escape a creature they have not seen

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! What object and light make the shadow.
variants.retryFeedback: Notice what Pico is carrying and what stands behind him.

illustration.alt: They check the coat’s shadow and discover mud and ribbon on a cart wheel.

lines: He moves the lantern beside the coat stand to show how its shadow changes.
The children can now see the light, the object, and the silhouette together.
blocks.title: Moving the lantern

lines: Nico touches the sleeve and laughs with relief.
What seemed like a creature was clothing; testing their idea gave them information that watching outside could not.
blocks.title: Just clothes

lines: Luna notices Pico's orange cart in a corner.
Its purple wheels hold mud from the same kind of path they followed from the place where the star hung.
blocks.title: The orange cart

lines: Blue ribbon with white dots hangs from a wheel.
Luna compares it with the scrap caught on the twig; the colour and pattern are the same.
blocks.title: Ribbon on the wheel

variants.prompt: What makes the shadow beside the lantern?

options.text: A coat stand with a coat

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! A coat stand with a coat.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for two matches: the marks on the ground and the blue fabric.

variants.prompt: What connects the cart to the trail?

options.text: Its muddy wheels and the matching ribbon

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! Its muddy wheels and the matching ribbon.
variants.retryFeedback: Look for two matches: the marks on the ground and the blue fabric.

illustration.alt: They connect the cart’s route to the hook and uncover a yellow point beneath cloth.

lines: They trace the two lines through the doorway to the cart.
Several observations now fit together, giving them a stronger lead than a single matching colour.
blocks.title: The same path

lines: Pico points towards the station hook and remembers moving his cart underneath it.
This explains the cart's route, but not yet the missing decoration's location.
blocks.title: Where it hung

lines: Luna lifts one corner of the striped cloth covering the load.
A yellow point appears below, and Nico leans closer to examine it before making another guess.
blocks.title: Lifting the cloth

lines: Part of a purple ring peeks out beside the point.
It reminds them of the star, but they must uncover the whole object and explain its journey.
blocks.title: What's peeking out?

variants.prompt: What peeks out beneath the cloth?

options.text: A yellow point and a purple ring

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! A yellow point and a purple ring.
variants.retryFeedback: Only part is visible. Think about how to check the rest.

variants.prompt: What should they do before saying it is the star?

options.text: Uncover and examine the whole object

variants.correctFeedback: That’s it! Uncover and examine the whole object.
variants.retryFeedback: Only part is visible. Think about how to check the rest.

ribbon.definition: A narrow strip of fabric used for tying or decorating.
ribbon.example: She tied a red ribbon around the gift before giving it away.

hook.definition: A curved piece used to hang something.
hook.example: We hung the keys on a hook by the door.

workshop.definition: A place where things are made or repaired.
workshop.example: We took the bike to the workshop because the chain had come off.

shadow.definition: A dark shape made when something blocks light.
shadow.example: We sat in the shadow of the tree to cool off.

silhouette.definition: The outline of a shape without its inner details.
silhouette.example: We recognized her silhouette against the light from the door.

lantern.definition: A light protected by a case that can be carried.
lantern.example: We carried a lantern to see the path in the dark.

sleeve.definition: The part of clothing that covers an arm.
sleeve.example: He rolled up his sleeve before washing his hands.

scrap.definition: A small piece left or torn from something.
scrap.example: He used a scrap of fabric to patch the torn backpack.

impression.definition: An early idea about what something seems like.
impression.example: Her first impression of the new student was that she was very shy.

decoration.definition: Something used to make a place look special.
decoration.example: We hung paper decorations around the classroom for the party.

investigate.definition: To look carefully for facts that explain something.
investigate.example: The detective decided to investigate the strange noise in the attic.
